# Endothelial density: is it over-called? Four causes, enumerated and tested

*Generated by `./.venv/bin/python -m tmesim.validation.endothelial_density`. Every number below is recomputed from the cached real bytes at run time. No file in `core/`, `physics/`, `sim/`, `reconstruct/real_xenium.py`, `reconstruct/vessel_network.py` or `reconstruct/vessel_geometry.py` was modified; this audit only calls them.*

## 0. Verdict first

| section | EC /mm2 (`matched_null_z`) | vs EM at 5 um (the reported over-call) | vs EM at the real sampling depth | **like-for-like: EC FRACTION vs H01 8.05%** | vs measured GBM cellularity x 8.05% | held-out purity |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | 154 | 7.0x | 2.8x | 1.30x | 0.44x | 67% |
| s2 | 645 | 29.4x | 12.4x | 0.88x | 1.84x | 43% |
| s3 | 757 | 34.5x | 15.3x | 1.09x | 2.16x | 70% |

**The reported 4-27x over-call is almost entirely a definitional mismatch.** (Recomputed against the same 5 um volume-EM reference under the CURRENT production classifier it is 7-35x; the published range came from the retired `mean_z` labels and mixed two reference values.) Three things are true simultaneously and they are usually conflated:

1. **(b) dominates.** The published comparison converts a 3-D volume-EM count into a section count with `N_A = N_V x t`, `t` = 5 um. The correct relation is `N_A = N_V x (t + h)` where `h` is the nuclear caliper height, because a Xenium cell exists whenever its nucleus is detected anywhere in the section. On these sections `t + h` is 12.5 / 11.8 / 11.3 um, i.e. **2.25-2.50x** the depth that was used. That factor alone removes 56-60% of the discrepancy, and it is arithmetic, not modelling.
2. **The residual factorises exactly**, into a depth-free ENDOTHELIAL FRACTION ratio (1.30 / 0.88 / 1.09x vs H01's 8.05% of cells) and a CELLULARITY ratio (2.1 / 14.2 / 14.1x), which is a statement about how hypercellular glioblastoma is and has nothing to do with endothelium. Measured GBM cellularity on 5 um H&E is 4,350 nuclei/mm2 against 1,107 in non-tumour brain (3.93x, PMID 24066240) — the same geometry as Xenium, no conversion needed. Against **that** reference (x H01's 8.05% endothelial) the sections read 0.44 / 1.84 / 2.16x — 1 of 3 sections BELOW the expectation.
3. **(a) is real and BOUNDED, but not negligible.** No cell on any section is labelled ENDOTHELIAL with zero endothelial transcripts — the specific red flag in the brief is absent, and it is absent *by construction* (§2). But a depth-matched held-out-gene mixture estimate puts label purity at 67 / 43 / 70%, i.e. 30-57% of the class is contamination, concentrated in the 1-transcript tier. That is a 1.43-2.34x over-call — material, but far short of 7-35x. Section 2 is the worst of the three and its estimate is also the least trustworthy; §2 says why its held-out probes are the weakest.

**(c) is a real defect but of a different quantity.** The 12 / 26 / 62 cells-per-cross-section figures are a linking-distance artefact: at 10 um linking the 99th percentile of `k` is 2.0 / 5.0 / 4.0 — inside Sargent's 1-6 on every section — and the maxima fall to 5.0 / 21.5 / 18.5; both explode only above 15 um. The linking distance **cannot** change the endothelial cell count — that is verified to the integer in §4 — so percolation contributes exactly zero to the density.

**(d) is CONFIRMED in direction, and it accounts for a minority of the elevation.** The Ivy GAP perivascular label is circular as it stands — its signature IS the endothelial gene set — but with every vascular and mural gene stripped from the signature panel it survives on the two dense sections and still concentrates endothelium: ~5% of the tissue at ~3x the endothelial fraction of the rest, holding ~10-13% of the endothelial cells (§5.1). Independently, the mural / pericyte programme — which shares no gene with the classifier — rises 1.5-5.8x from the lowest to the highest endothelial-density decile, exactly as Ivy GAP's definition of CTmvp ("a common vessel wall of endothelial AND SMOOTH MUSCLE cells") requires. So the excess is real, focally concentrated vascular structure — but the perivascular zones hold only ~10% of the endothelial cells, so microvascular proliferation is not where most of the count comes from.

## 1. What the number is, exactly

**Definition.** *Endothelial density* = the number of measured Xenium cell objects whose marker-derived `CellType` is `ENDOTHELIAL`, divided by the area of the geometric tissue mask (`real_xenium.tissue_mask_from_cells`, the union of 30 um discs around the measured centroids) at `dx = 12 um`. A *measured cell object* is one **flattened 2-D segmentation polygon** produced by 10x Xenium Onboard Analysis from the DAPI nucleus stack of a nominally **5 um** FFPE section, with transcripts assigned to it **by x-y coordinate only**. So the quantity is a 2-D PROFILE COUNT of nuclei present in a thin slab, per unit slab area.

Two denominators are in circulation in this repo and they differ by 1.4-1.5x: `results/vessel_geometry_fix.md` divides by the tissue mask (used here), `results/classifier_fix.md` by the bounding box. Both are given below.

| section | typing rule | cells | ENDOTHELIAL | ENDO % | tissue mm2 | **EC /mm2 (tissue)** | EC /mm2 (bbox) | all cells /mm2 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | `mean_z` *(legacy)* | 40,887 | 3,984 | 9.74 | 27.9 | **143** | 97 | 1,465 |
|  | `matched_null_z` **(production)** | 40,887 | 4,295 | 10.50 | 27.9 | **154** | 105 | 1,465 |
| s2 | `mean_z` *(legacy)* | 816,769 | 34,179 | 4.18 | 89.5 | **382** | 275 | 9,127 |
|  | `matched_null_z` **(production)** | 816,769 | 57,733 | 7.07 | 89.5 | **645** | 465 | 9,127 |
| s3 | `mean_z` *(legacy)* | 851,509 | 103,817 | 12.19 | 98.5 | **1,054** | 687 | 8,647 |
|  | `matched_null_z` **(production)** | 851,509 | 74,515 | 8.75 | 98.5 | **757** | 493 | 8,647 |

**First finding, before any of the four causes.** The headline 143 / 382 / 1054 per mm2 in `results/vessel_geometry_fix.md` are the **LEGACY `mean_z`** labels — the arity-biased rule that `results/classifier_fix.md` retired. Under the production default `matched_null_z` the same sections read 154 / 645 / 757 per mm2. Section 2 moves by 1.7x. Any downstream number quoted against 382 /mm2 is quoting a rule that is no longer in force; both are carried through every table below rather than picking one.

### The section's own geometry, measured from the cell table

| section | mean nucleus profile um2 | equiv. nuclear diameter h (um) | **effective depth t+h (um)** | mean cell polygon um2 | segmented area / tissue area | nuclear profile area fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | 44.5 | 7.52 | 12.52 | 497.8 | 0.730 | 0.065 |
| s2 | 36.7 | 6.84 | 11.84 | 83.1 | 0.758 | 0.335 |
| s3 | 30.9 | 6.27 | 11.27 | 97.7 | 0.845 | 0.267 |

`h` is the equivalent-circle diameter of the mean observed nucleus PROFILE, which is a **lower bound** on the true mean nuclear caliper (a slab cuts most nuclei off-centre). The bound's direction is deliberate: a larger `h` would make the literature prediction larger and the apparent over-call smaller, so the conservative choice is used throughout.

The mean cell polygon differs 6x between section 1 (498 um2) and sections 2-3 (83 / 98 um2). That is a segmentation-version difference, not a tissue difference: 10x XOA <= v1.9 expanded nuclei isotropically by **15 um**, v2.0 by **5 um** (10x doc CG000750). It matters here because a 15 um expansion collects transcripts from ~1.5 cell diameters away, which is the mechanism the spillover probe in §2 tests.

## 2. (a) Marker-positivity audit: are the labelled cells endothelial?

The brief's red flag is "a cell called endothelial with zero endothelial transcripts". **There are none, on any section, under either rule.**

| section | rule | gated markers | n ENDOTHELIAL | with >=1 marker transcript | **with ZERO** | marker+ base rate (all cells) | marker+ among NON-endothelial |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | `mean_z` | PECAM1 | 3,984 | 100.00% | **0.00%** | 24.6% | 16.4% |
|  | `matched_null_z` | PECAM1 | 4,295 | 100.00% | **0.00%** | 24.6% | 15.7% |
| s2 | `mean_z` | VWF, FLT1, PLVAP | 34,179 | 100.00% | **0.00%** | 13.1% | 9.3% |
|  | `matched_null_z` | VWF, FLT1, PLVAP | 57,733 | 100.00% | **0.00%** | 13.1% | 6.5% |
| s3 | `mean_z` | PECAM1 | 103,817 | 100.00% | **0.00%** | 14.0% | 2.1% |
|  | `matched_null_z` | PECAM1 | 74,515 | 100.00% | **0.00%** | 14.0% | 5.8% |

The zero column is 0.00% everywhere, and that is **not a coincidence or a pass mark** — it is forced. Every scoring rule in `phenotype_cells` is monotone increasing in the marker z-scores, a zero-count cell sits at the minimum of every marker's z, and the gate at 1.0 is above that minimum. So this test can never fail as posed, and it is reported to close the hypothesis rather than to support the labels. The informative question is not *whether* there is a transcript but *how many*.

The pattern is the same on all three sections and it is the finding of (a): **held-out positivity is strongly graded by marker count.** The >=5-transcript tier is 50-100% positive for genes the classifier never saw. The absolute level varies enormously between sections because the probes' own SENSITIVITY does — FLT1 is detected in 17% of all section-1 cells, section 2's SOX17 in 1.4% — which is exactly why the purity estimate below reads `p_trueEC` off the SAME probe rather than assuming a probe detects every endothelial cell: the probe's sensitivity then cancels out of the mixture, and only its SPECIFICITY has to hold. The 1-transcript tier is far weaker, and it is the tier the two rules disagree most about: on section 1 the legacy `mean_z` rule admitted none of it (its gate on a single PECAM1 marker is effectively a >= 2-count rule there), while `matched_null_z` admits a third of the class from it.

### Held-out genes, one at a time

One broadly expressed gene could manufacture an enrichment, so the probe is broken out per gene. Enrichment = P(gene+ | ENDOTHELIAL) / P(gene+ | not ENDOTHELIAL). Genes marked *report-only* (:data:`HELDOUT_REPORT_ONLY` = A2M) are shown but EXCLUDED from the pooled probe and from the purity estimate, on a prior judgement about their specificity rather than on how they scored — selecting probes by their enrichment in the class under test would be circular.

| section | held-out gene | panel detection rate | % positive among ENDOTHELIAL | % positive among the rest | enrichment |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | FLT1 | 17.0% | 64.9% | 11.4% | **5.69x** |
| s2 | SOX17 | 1.4% | 9.8% | 0.7% | **13.19x** |
| s2 | RAMP2 | 4.8% | 17.2% | 3.9% | **4.41x** |
| s2 | ACKR1 | 3.4% | 2.4% | 3.5% | **0.68x** |
| s2 | SELE | 0.2% | 0.3% | 0.2% | **1.17x** |
| s2 | A2M *(report-only)* | 51.4% | 74.7% | 49.7% | **1.50x** |
| s3 | CD34 | 12.4% | 58.8% | 8.0% | **7.37x** |
| s3 | CLDN5 | 9.6% | 51.5% | 5.6% | **9.22x** |
| s3 | VWF | 10.8% | 53.6% | 6.7% | **7.95x** |
| s3 | PLVAP | 6.3% | 21.7% | 4.8% | **4.48x** |
| s3 | KDR | 9.0% | 50.6% | 5.0% | **10.09x** |
| s3 | FLT1 | 10.9% | 53.8% | 6.7% | **7.98x** |
| s3 | ACKR1 | 5.0% | 3.6% | 5.2% | **0.70x** |
| s3 | DLL4 | 5.2% | 33.5% | 2.5% | **13.48x** |

The weakest held-out gene on each section is the counter-example that shows the test has teeth: `FLT1` on s1 (enrichment 5.69x at a 17% panel detection rate); `ACKR1` on s2 (enrichment 0.68x at a 3% panel detection rate); `ACKR1` on s3 (enrichment 0.70x at a 5% panel detection rate). A broadly expressed gene carries no information, so the conclusion rests on the specific ones. Section 2 is the weakest of the three on this test for a structural reason — its endothelial programme (VWF / FLT1 / PLVAP) and its held-out set are both on the same immuno-oncology panel and are less specific than PECAM1 + CD34 / CLDN5 / KDR.

### Purity: a depth-matched mixture estimate

Treating the labelled class as a mixture of true endothelium (fraction `f`) and background, and reading `f` off a held-out gene: `f = (p_labelled - p_background) / (p_trueEC - p_background)`, with `p_trueEC` from the >=5-transcript tier, pooling only the probe genes (report-only genes excluded). Computed **inside total-count deciles and then pooled**, because held-out positivity rises with a cell's sequencing depth and the high-confidence tier is deep by construction — an unmatched estimate is biased low.

| section | rule | p(held-out+) labelled | p background | p high-confidence | **depth-matched purity** | unmatched (for comparison) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | `mean_z` | 67.5% | 11.6% | 92.1% | **70%** | 70% |
|  | `matched_null_z` | 64.9% | 11.4% | 96.4% | **67%** | 63% |
| s2 | `mean_z` | 39.2% | 8.0% | 49.1% | **78%** | 76% |
|  | `matched_null_z` | 25.2% | 8.1% | 49.7% | **43%** | 41% |
| s3 | `mean_z` | 74.4% | 26.8% | 99.9% | **65%** | 65% |
|  | `matched_null_z` | 78.3% | 28.2% | 99.9% | **70%** | 70% |

**The sharpest single result in (a) is in the tier table, not here.** Held-out positivity in the **1-transcript tier**, against that section's background: s1 34.0% vs 11.4% (2.98x); s2 6.6% vs 8.1% (0.81x); s3 55.2% vs 28.2% (1.96x). On sections 1 and 3 that tier is 2-3x enriched — diluted, but real endothelium is in it. On section 2 it is **at or below background**, i.e. the ~23,500 cells the production rule admits on one endothelial transcript carry no independent endothelial evidence whatever. That is the whole of section 2's purity deficit, and it is the one place in this audit where a concrete over-call is localised to a specific, countable set of cells.

**Section 2's absolute purity number is still the least reliable.** Its probes are extremely sparse (SOX17 1.4%, SELE 0.2% of all cells), so `p_trueEC` is only ~50% and both the numerator and the denominator of the mixture are small differences between small numbers. The direction is solid; the second digit is not. This is the same structural problem `results/classifier_fix.md` §6 item 1 identifies for that section — the immuno-oncology panel has no endothelial gene as specific as PECAM1 — and it limits what any audit of it can conclude, including this one.

**Two residual biases, in opposite directions, and neither is removed.** `p_trueEC` is still an upper bound after depth matching, because marker count and held-out count correlate for reasons beyond depth (a cell with ten PECAM1 transcripts is a *more central* endothelial cell, not just a deeper one) — that biases purity DOWN. And `p_background` is contaminated by every true endothelial cell the classifier MISSED, which biases purity UP. The honest reading is therefore the order of magnitude, not the second digit: **43-70% of the labelled class is supported by independent marker evidence**, i.e. the classifier over-calls by 1.43-2.34x, concentrated entirely in the 1-transcript tier.

### Is the weak tier just transcript spillover?

Section 1's segmentation expands each nucleus by 15 um, so a cell abutting a vessel can inherit a stray endothelial transcript. Test: are the 1-transcript calls closer to strong (>=5-transcript) endothelial cells than a random non-endothelial cell is?

| section | n 1-count calls | % of class | median dist to strong EC (um) | same, random control | % within 20 um | control % within 20 um | n isolated (>30 um) | isolated: held-out+ | background held-out+ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | 1,474 | 34% | 84 | 98 | 11.3% | 3.0% | 1,163 | 28.0% | 11.4% |
| s2 | 23,470 | 41% | 34 | 49 | 27.9% | 12.6% | 13,097 | 6.7% | 8.1% |
| s3 | 32,070 | 43% | 36 | 49 | 25.9% | 11.4% | 18,574 | 48.7% | 28.2% |

Spillover is present but is **not** the main mechanism: the 1-count calls are 2.2-3.8x more likely than a control cell to sit within 20 um of a strong endothelial cell, yet the large majority of them are >30 um from any strong endothelial cell. Those ISOLATED weak calls carry s1 2.46x; s2 0.83x; s3 1.73x the background held-out positivity — real but diluted endothelium on sections 1 and 3, and NOTHING above background on section 2, the same split §2's tier table shows. So the weak tier is a genuine mixture on two sections and close to pure background on the third. This test is suggestive, not decisive on its own: a second endothelial cell in the same vessel wall is *also* adjacent to a strong one, so proximity cannot distinguish bleed from biology — only the held-out probe can.

## 3. (b) Definitional reconciliation: the two numbers count different things

### What each side counts

| | H01 volume EM | Xenium |
|---|---|---|
| one unit is | one endothelial cell, identified and traced in **3-D** | one **flattened 2-D polygon** per DAPI-detected nucleus |
| support | 1.05 mm3 of tissue (5,019 sections at 33.9 nm, reassembled) | one nominally **5 um** FFPE section, x-y area |
| counting rule | "all the cells with nuclei in the sample, manually identifying and quantifying them" — volumetric, no profile bias | transcripts assigned **by x-y coordinate only**; a cell exists if its nucleus is detected anywhere in the section |
| tissue | normal-appearing human temporal cortex | human glioblastoma |
| what it yields | a number density per mm3 | a profile count per mm2 |

So the two are not comparable without a conversion, and the conversion is the **profile-counting (DeHoff / Abercrombie) relation**

```
    N_A = N_V x (t + h)        t = section thickness, h = caliper height
                               of the object being counted (the nucleus)
```

The reported comparison used `N_A = N_V x t` with `t` = 5 um, giving **21.9 EC/mm2** (the "~22 /mm2"). Dropping `h` is not a small approximation here: the measured nuclear profiles on these sections are 6.3-7.5 um across, so `h` EXCEEDS `t` and the prediction is low by a factor **(t+h)/t = 2.25-2.50x**.

### The forward prediction, and the exact factorisation

| section | t+h (um) | H01 pred. EC/mm2 at t only | H01 pred. EC/mm2 at t+h | H01 pred. all cells/mm2 | obs. EC/mm2 | obs. cells/mm2 | ratio (naive) | ratio (depth-corrected) | **x fraction ratio** | x cellularity ratio | = product (check) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | 12.5 | 21.9 | 54.9 | 682 | 154 | 1,465 | 7.0x | 2.80x | **1.30x** | 2.15x | 2.80x |
| s2 | 11.8 | 21.9 | 51.9 | 645 | 645 | 9,127 | 29.4x | 12.43x | **0.88x** | 14.16x | 12.43x |
| s3 | 11.3 | 21.9 | 49.4 | 614 | 757 | 8,647 | 34.5x | 15.32x | **1.09x** | 14.09x | 15.32x |

The last three columns are an identity, not three measurements: `obs_EC/pred_EC = (obs EC% / H01 EC%) x (obs cells per mm2 / pred cells per mm2)`, and the product column confirms it to the last digit. **Only the middle factor is a claim about the endothelial call.** The right-hand factor is a statement about cellularity and effective sampling depth, shared by every cell type in the section, and it is where 2.1-14.2x of the discrepancy lives.

H01 reference values used, all quoted: 4,604 endothelial cells and 57,180 cells total in 1.05 mm3 = **8.05% of cells endothelial**, 4,385 EC/mm3, 54,457 cells/mm3, 230 mm of vessel = 219 mm/mm3 and 20.0 EC per mm of vessel (PMID 38723085, [doi](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adk4858)).

### Like-for-like #1 — the endothelial FRACTION (needs no assumption at all)

The endothelial fraction of all cells is dimensionless: it does not involve the section thickness, the nuclear caliper, the tissue-area denominator or the segmentation's cell size. It is the one number the two assays can be compared on directly.

| section | rule | ENDOTHELIAL % of cells | vs H01 normal cortex (8.05%) | vs independent Visium NNLS (9.77%) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | `mean_z` | 9.74% | 1.21x | 1.00x |
|  | `matched_null_z` | 10.50% | 1.30x | 1.08x |
| s2 | `mean_z` | 4.18% | 0.52x | 0.43x |
|  | `matched_null_z` | 7.07% | 0.88x | 0.72x |
| s3 | `mean_z` | 12.19% | 1.51x | 1.25x |
|  | `matched_null_z` | 8.75% | 1.09x | 0.90x |

**This is the answer to the brief's question.** Compared like-for-like, the sections sit at 0.88-1.30x a normal-cortex endothelial fraction and 0.72-1.08x an independent, gate-free NNLS deconvolution of a real GBM Visium sample (`results/classifier_fix.md` §5, quoted not recomputed). There is no 4-27x. The Visium comparison is the more appropriate one — it is tumour, not cortex — and a GBM at ~1.0x the normal-cortex endothelial *fraction* is entirely expected even though its vasculature is grossly abnormal, because hypercellularity inflates the denominator at the same time as neoangiogenesis inflates the numerator.

### Like-for-like #2 — against MEASURED GBM cellularity on 5 um sections

The cellularity factor should not have to be taken on trust, and it does not have to be: nuclear density has been measured on 5 um H&E sections — the same geometry as Xenium, so no depth conversion enters — with a matched non-tumour control arm. **4,350 nuclei/mm2 in high-grade glioma against 1,107 in non-tumour brain = 3.93x** (Boruah D & Deb P, ISRN Oncol 2013;2013:760653, PMID 24066240, [doi](https://doi.org/10.1155/2013/760653)); corroborated at 4,557 +/- 3,169 cells/mm2 over 561 stereotactic GBM biopsies (PMID 28103256, [doi](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0169292)), i.e. two independent studies within 5%.

| section | obs. cells/mm2 | vs measured GBM 4,350/mm2 | expected EC/mm2 = 4,350 x 8.05% | obs. EC/mm2 | **ratio** | expected EC/mm2 = 4,350 x 9.77% (Visium) | ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | 1,465 | 0.34x | 350 | 154 | **0.44x** | 425 | 0.36x |
| s2 | 9,127 | 2.10x | 350 | 645 | **1.84x** | 425 | 1.52x |
| s3 | 8,647 | 1.99x | 350 | 757 | **2.16x** | 425 | 1.78x |

Observed / expected is 0.44 / 1.84 / 2.16x, i.e. a span of 0.44-2.16x with 1 of 3 sections BELOW the expectation. The caveat on this anchor is stated in its own paper: both arms were measured in fields selected for *maximum* cellularity, so the 4,350 figure is an upper-ish estimate and these ratios are correspondingly conservative in the direction of under-calling.

### Like-for-like #3 — the vessel side, with no cell-type call at all

For an isotropic curve network cut by a plane, `L_V = 2 N_A`, so the number of vessel TRANSECTS a thin section shows per unit area is `L_V / 2` — which is exactly what a CD31/CD34 microvessel-density count measures. This tests the vascular geometry without using the endothelial labels for anything except clustering.

| section | MVD /mm2 (this reconstruction, 20 um linking) | L_V/2, H01 | L_V/2, independent stereology | L_V/2 x GBM vascular enrichment (3.62x) | implied EC per mm of vessel | **vs H01's 20/mm** |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | 111 | 110 | 128 | 462 | 55.5 | **2.77x** |
| s2 | 233 | 110 | 128 | 462 | 116.8 | **5.84x** |
| s3 | 320 | 110 | 128 | 462 | 104.8 | **5.24x** |

Independent human normal-cortex stereology gives L_V = 255 +/- 119 mm/mm3 and microvessel N_V = 1,311 +/- 326 /mm3 (Kubikova T et al., J Chem Neuroanat 2017;88:22-32, PMID 29113946, [doi](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jchemneu.2017.11.005)), against 219 mm/mm3 derived from H01 — the two normal-cortex anchors agree to 14%, well inside one SD, so the reference is not resting on a single dataset. GBM's vascular enrichment factor is the measured CD34+ area ratio, 2.1% vs 0.58% (PMID 36611806, [doi](https://doi.org/10.3390/cells12010011)).

**The vessel-object density is right, and it is the strongest positive result in this report.** The sections land at 111 / 233 / 320 vessel objects per mm2 against 110-128 for normal cortex and 462 for cortex scaled by GBM's measured vascular enrichment — i.e. between the normal-cortex and the tumour expectation, which is where a GBM resection should be. Nothing here supports a 7-35x error in the vasculature.

What *is* elevated is **endothelial nuclei per unit vessel length**: 2.8-5.8x H01's measured 20 per mm. Two readings, and this report cannot separate them: endothelial hyperplasia / multilayering (which is what microvascular proliferation *is* histologically — Ivy GAP defines CThbv as "increased density of blood vessels that appear to have thickened walls (endothelial cell proliferation)"), or the 1.43-2.34x classifier over-call from (a) compounded with `L_V = 2 x MVD` under-estimating vessel length wherever (c) has merged transects into one object. Both push this number up.

## 4. (c) Linking-distance sweep: percolation is real, and it cannot move the density

`vessel_network.segment_vessels` groups endothelial cells by single-linkage at `LINK_DISTANCE_UM` = 20 um (exactly `DBSCAN(eps=20, min_samples=1)`), and `vessel_geometry.vessel_geometry` derives cells-per-cross-section as `k = N / max(1, extent / 50 um)`. The reported maxima of 12 / 26 / 62 are the tail of that `k`. Sweeping the linking distance:

*Method note: the sweep groups clusters by sorting the labels rather than by masking, because production `segment_vessels` is `O(n_objects x n_endothelial)` and that is 10^10 element comparisons per linking distance on the densest section. Every quantity in the tables above is checked against `segment_vessels` itself at the production 20 um on every section: **identical on all of them**.*

**Four things this establishes.**

1. **The endothelial cell count is identical across the whole sweep** (the `EC cells` column never moves; checked programmatically at run time: every section returns a single distinct value over all 7 linking distances). The linking distance is a statement about how the SAME cells are grouped. So percolation contributes **exactly zero** to the density that is the subject of this report, and (c) can be ruled out as a cause of the 4-27x by construction, not by measurement.
2. **The `k` explosion is a linking-distance artefact.** At 10 um linking the 99th percentile of `k` is 2.0 / 5.0 / 4.0 — inside Sargent's 1-6 on every section — and the maxima are 5.0 / 21.5 / 18.5, so section 1's distribution is entirely defensible there and sections 2-3 have a thin tail above the reference. At the production 20 um the maxima are 12.8 / 28.4 / 41.5 and 6.0 / 11.8 / 9.7, and the largest object's in-plane extent grows from 19 / 71 / 81 um to 154 / 497 / 678 um over the same step. An object of a millimetre's extent is not a vessel cross-section.
3. **Percolation is entering, but the section is nowhere near a global giant component.** The mean number of other endothelial cells within the linking distance reaches only 0.71 / 2.35 / 1.74 at 20 um against the 2-D random-geometric-graph threshold of 4.512, and the largest object holds 0.29-0.76% of the endothelial cells. So this is *local* over-merging of neighbouring transects, not a network-wide collapse — which is why the fraction of endothelial cells sitting in `k > 6` objects is 7 / 45 / 29% across the three sections.
4. **`k` is not comparable to Sargent's count in the first place.** Sargent SM et al., Vasc Biol 2023;5(1) (PMID 37582180, [doi](https://doi.org/10.1530/VB-23-0010)) counts endothelial cells whose **wall** is present in a cross-section, traced in 3-D in **NORMAL MOUSE** cortex. `k` here counts endothelial **nuclei whose centre lies inside a ~12 um slab**, grouped by proximity. In normal cortex those are not the same number: H01's 20 EC per mm of vessel over a 12.5 um sampling depth predicts about **0.5 endothelial nuclei per vessel profile**, i.e. half of all vessel transects in a normal-cortex Xenium section would contain no endothelial nucleus at all and be invisible to a marker-based cell call. Comparing 12 against 5-6 compares a nucleus count in a slab against a wall-cell count in a traced cross-section.

**And the GBM-side reference the earlier report did not have.** A glomeruloid microvascular-proliferation tuft is *defined* as "clustered vessels embedded within a connective stroma with a glomerulus-like appearance (containing 15-100 nuclei)" (Soni N et al., J Pathol Transl Med 2024;58(3):127-133, PMID 38766738, [doi](https://doi.org/10.4132/jptm.2024.03.11)), and Ivy GAP defines CTmvp as "two or more blood vessels sharing a common vessel wall of endothelial and smooth muscle cells", appearing either as a glomerulus ~100 um across **or as a garland of interconnected vessels 50 um x 1 to 6 MILLIMETRES**. So on a GBM section a single legitimate vascular object may contain tens of nuclei and span a millimetre. Object extent alone cannot condemn a segmentation here, and an object of a few tens of cells is inside the published range for a real structure. What is *not* defensible is the largest objects at 20 um linking — 23 / 165 / 563 cells, up to 6x the top of the glomeruloid range.

## 5. (d) Is the excess regionally concentrated? The GBM-biology test

Microvascular proliferation is diagnostic of glioblastoma, so a GBM section SHOULD exceed normal cortex; the question is *by how much and where*. If the excess sits in a minority of the tissue with the histology of microvascular proliferation, it is signal. If it is spread uniformly, it is error.

### 5.1 The Ivy GAP region labelling is CIRCULAR here, and the test shows it

Each section is binned at 100 um (the diameter Ivy GAP quotes for a glomeruloid structure), each bin's cells are summed into one pseudo-spot, and the spot is labelled by Spearman correlation against the REAL Ivy GAP per-anatomic-structure signatures (`reconstruct/region_label.py`). The Ivy GAP `perivascular` signature is built on PECAM1 / VWF / CD34 / CLDN5 / FLT1 — **the same genes the classifier gates ENDOTHELIAL on**. So the labelling is run twice: once as-is, and once with every vascular, mural and vascular-basement-membrane gene stripped from the signature panel.

**s1** — 1,982 bins of 100 um with >= 10 cells; 41 shared signature genes, 33 after stripping (CAV1, CD36, COL1A2, DCN, FLT1, IGFBP3, IGFBP4, PECAM1)

| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

*full_panel*: perivascular bins are 27.1% of the tissue and hold 45.9% of the endothelial cells (16.4% endothelial inside them vs 6.3% elsewhere). Setting them to the rest of the tissue's endothelial fraction would remove only **28.4%** of the endothelial cells.

**The circularity is large and it is measurable.** With the vascular genes stripped the `perivascular` label falls to 0.0-5.2% of bins, from 0.5-27.1% with them. The label was carrying (almost) no non-vascular evidence: it was the endothelial gene set, relabelled. And even in the circular version the perivascular bins are 0.5-27.1% of the tissue and account for 1.9-45.9% of the endothelial cells, so they could not explain the density either way. **But the stripped version is a valid test, and on the two dense sections it PASSES**: a `perivascular` label built with no vascular, mural or vascular-basement-membrane gene in its panel still lands on ~5% of bins that carry ~3x the endothelial fraction of the rest of the tissue. That is genuine, non-circular evidence that endothelium concentrates in independently-identified perivascular zones. What it is NOT is an explanation of the density: those zones hold ~10-13% of the endothelial cells, so removing their excess would move the section total by well under 10%.

Section 1 is the exception, and the reason is its panel rather than the method: the 319-gene brain panel carries no mural / pericyte programme at all (§5.3 finds only CSPG4 on it) and shares few of the Ivy GAP perivascular signature's genes to begin with, so once PECAM1 and FLT1 go there is nothing distinctively perivascular left for a bin to correlate with. That is a limit on what section 1 can be asked, not evidence that it has no perivascular zones.

### 5.2 Label-free: are the endothelial cells clustered?

| section | occupied 100 um bins | mean EC/bin | Gini(EC) | Gini(all cells) | Gini(Poisson null) | top-decile share of EC | same, all cells | same, Poisson null | bins with no EC |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

Endothelial cells are substantially more unevenly distributed than cells in general and than a Poisson null at the same mean — so the class is spatially structured, not scattered. This rules out the *shape* of a diffuse classifier error, but it does not identify the structures as microvascular proliferation: ordinary capillaries are clustered too.

### 5.3 Non-circular: do independent programmes track the excess?

Bins are ranked into deciles by local endothelial density, and three gene programmes that share **no gene** with any endothelial marker or held-out probe are scored per decile (counts per 10,000 total counts in the bin, so bin depth and cell number cancel). Ivy GAP's own definition of CTmvp requires **smooth-muscle cells** in the shared vessel wall, so genuine microvascular proliferation must carry a mural programme; GBM neoangiogenesis is driven from perinecrotic hypoxia; and CThbv is *defined* by endothelial proliferation.

**The mural result is the strong one, and it is monotone.** The pericyte / smooth-muscle programme rises 1.47-5.77x from the lowest to the highest endothelial-density decile — 3.24-5.77x on the two sections whose panels actually measure a mural programme (RGS5 / PDGFRB / NOTCH3 / ACTA2 and friends; section 1's brain panel has only CSPG4, which is why its gradient is the weakest). It increases at every decile, not just at the top. Since the classifier cannot see any of these genes, this is independent evidence that the high-endothelial bins contain real, mural-invested vessels — exactly what Ivy GAP's "common vessel wall of endothelial and smooth muscle cells" describes — and it is not what a diffuse labelling error would produce.

**Hypoxia does NOT track endothelial density, and on section 2 it runs the other way** (s1: 1.33x, s2: 0.39x, s3: 1.05x). That is the expected sign once the scale is taken seriously: a 100 um bin dense in vessels is a WELL-PERFUSED bin, so its HIF-response programme should be low even though microvascular proliferation is, at the tissue scale, driven by perinecrotic hypoxia. The prediction stated at the head of this subsection was the wrong way round; the measurement is reported as it came out. Proliferation is flat to slightly negative (1.15x, 1.09x, 0.93x), which does not support "endothelial proliferation" being detectable as a bin-level cell-cycle signal against a background of proliferating tumour.

**One confound that is not removed.** The top endothelial decile also carries 1.39-2.39x the total cell density of the bottom decile, so some of the mural gradient is cellularity rather than vascular identity. The per-10,000-count normalisation removes bin depth and cell number but not composition.

**Verdict on (d).** Three independent lines agree that the excess is real, focal vascular structure and not a diffuse labelling error: a vascular-gene-free Ivy GAP perivascular label still finds ~5% of bins at ~3x the endothelial fraction of the rest; endothelial cells are far more clustered than cells in general and than a Poisson null; and an unseen mural programme rises monotonically with endothelial density, up to 5.8x. **But (d) does not explain the number.** The perivascular zones hold ~10-13% of the endothelial cells, and setting them to the rest of the tissue's endothelial fraction moves the section total by under 10%. Microvascular proliferation is present, independently identifiable, and a MINORITY contributor to the count.

Quantifying it properly needs the CTmvp / CThbv annotations themselves — Ivy GAP's ~12,000 machine-annotated H&E images expose per-block normalised areas through its API — rather than a transcriptional proxy whose signature overlaps the thing being measured. That is a data acquisition task, not an analysis one, and it is not done here.

## 6. Verdict: how much is artefact, how much is biology

### The budget

| section | reported over-call | of which: DEPTH (definitional) | of which: CELLULARITY (definitional, not endothelial) | residual: EC fraction vs normal cortex | of which: classifier over-call (1/purity) | biologically attributable residual |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| s1 | 7.0x | 2.50x | 2.15x | 1.30x | 1.50x | 0.87x |
| s2 | 29.4x | 2.37x | 14.16x | 0.88x | 2.34x | 0.38x |
| s3 | 34.5x | 2.25x | 14.09x | 1.09x | 1.43x | 0.76x |

Read left to right: the reported factor is the product of the first three columns (identically, §3), of which the first two are definitional and carry no information about endothelium. The fourth column is the only endothelial claim, and the fifth says 30-57% of it is classifier contamination. What is left is the last column: **the endothelial fraction of these GBM sections, corrected for the estimated label impurity, is 0.38-0.87x that of normal human cortex.**

### Answers, one line each

| candidate | verdict |
|---|---|
| **(a) classifier over-calling** | REAL AND BOUNDED. Zero cells are labelled endothelial with no endothelial transcript (and cannot be, by construction). Held-out endothelial genes are enriched 5.7 / 3.1 / 2.8x in the labelled class. Depth-matched purity 67 / 43 / 70%, i.e. a **1.43-2.34x** over-call, entirely in the 1-transcript tier. Accounts for 1.43-2.34x of a 7-35x claim. |
| **(b) definitional mismatch** | **THE DOMINANT CAUSE — there is no 7-35x bug.** The comparison was 3-D volumetric counts vs 2-D profile counts, converted with the wrong depth (`t` instead of `t+h`, a 2.25-2.50x error), and then divided by a cellularity difference that is not about endothelium. Like-for-like the sections sit at 0.88-1.30x normal cortex's endothelial FRACTION and 0.44-2.16x the density predicted from measured GBM cellularity. |
| **(c) segmentation percolation** | REAL, but of a DIFFERENT quantity. It inflates `k` (max 12.8 / 28.4 / 41.5 at 20 um linking; 5.0 / 21.5 / 18.5 at 10 um) and cannot change the cell count by a single cell — verified across the whole sweep. Contributes **exactly 0x** to the density. Separately, `k` was never comparable to Sargent's 5-6 (normal MOUSE cortex, wall cells in a 3-D-traced cross-section vs nuclei in a 12 um slab). |
| **(d) GBM biology** | CONFIRMED IN DIRECTION, MINORITY CONTRIBUTOR. The Ivy GAP perivascular label is circular as it stands, but a version with every vascular and mural gene stripped from its panel survives on the two dense sections and still finds ~5% of bins at ~3x the endothelial fraction of the rest, holding only ~10-13% of the endothelial cells. An unseen mural / pericyte programme rises 1.5-5.8x from the lowest to the highest endothelial-density decile, monotonically. Endothelial cells are far more clustered than cells in general and than Poisson. The vessel-object density lands between the normal-cortex and GBM-scaled expectations. Endothelial nuclei per mm of vessel is 2.8-5.8x H01's 20/mm, which is what "thickened walls (endothelial cell proliferation)" means — but that estimate inherits both (a) and (c) as upward biases. |

### What to change

**1. Retire the "~22 endothelial cells per mm2" comparison and the "4-27x over-call" claim.** They are in `results/vessel_geometry_fix.md` §5 item 1 and they are not a like-for-like comparison. Replace with the endothelial FRACTION against H01's 8.05% and against the Visium NNLS 9.77%, both of which the reconstruction already satisfies to 0.88-1.30x. Also retire the "objects with implausible cells-per-cross-section" framing against Sargent's 5-6: the reference is normal mouse cortex measured a different way, and the GBM reference (15-100 nuclei per glomeruloid tuft) goes the other way.

**2. The numbers in `results/vessel_geometry_fix.md` are LEGACY-classifier numbers and should be regenerated.** 143 / 382 / 1054 EC/mm2 and MVD 111 / 104 / 358 were computed under `aggregation='mean_z'`, which `results/classifier_fix.md` retired; the production default gives 154 / 645 / 757 EC/mm2 and MVD 111 / 233 / 320. Section 2 moves 1.7x, which breaks that report's "sections 1 and 2 have near-identical vessel densities" observation and the inference drawn from it. This is a re-run, not a code change.

**3. `LINK_DISTANCE_UM = 20` is too permissive on the dense sections and should be revisited — but not by tuning it to `k`.** At 20 um, 7 / 45 / 29% of each section's endothelial cells sit in objects with `k > 6`, and the largest objects hold 23 / 165 / 563 cells (up to 6x the top of the published glomeruloid range). At 10 um every section's `k` distribution is defensible. The honest fix is not a new constant but a criterion: an object should be split when its point cloud is not consistent with one tube or one ~100 um tuft. **Not changed here** — `vessel_network.py` is out of scope for this audit and other agents are active in the tree.

**4. The 1-transcript tier is where the whole over-call lives, and on section 2 it is indefensible.** It is 34 / 41 / 43% of the class. On sections 1 and 3 it is 2-3x enriched for held-out endothelial genes (real endothelium, diluted); on section 2 it sits AT OR BELOW background (~23,500 cells with no independent endothelial evidence at all). The change with the best evidence behind it is therefore section-2-specific rather than a global count floor. Requiring >= 2 endothelial marker transcripts globally would raise purity toward the >=3-transcript tiers' 20-100% held-out positivity at the cost of losing genuine low-expressing endothelium. This is a real trade-off and this report does not recommend making it unilaterally: the `matched_null_z` fix admitted that tier deliberately, to remove the arity bias, and a hard count floor would reintroduce a panel-dependent threshold of exactly the kind that bug was about. It should be decided with the delivery-side sensitivity in hand.

**5. Nothing here justifies rescaling the vascular source term.** The quantity that drives delivery is the vascular field, and its two load-bearing properties — vessel-object density and the spatial distribution of vasculature — are within a factor of ~1 of independent human anchors. A correction of the order this audit supports (1.43-2.34x on the endothelial count, from the weak tier) is smaller than the factor-3.6 radius-model spread `results/vessel_geometry_fix.md` §5 already reports as the dominant uncertainty on the area fraction.

### What this audit did NOT resolve

1. **The absolute effective sampling depth.** `t + h` uses the vendor nominal 5 um and a *lower bound* on `h`. The true `h` is larger, which would push the H01 prediction up and the residual down further. Nothing here measures the actual depth of these blocks.
2. **The 2.8-5.8x endothelial nuclei per mm of vessel.** Multilayering, classifier impurity and merged transects all push it up and this report cannot separate them. Separating them needs a vessel segmentation that is not single-linkage on endothelial nuclei.
3. **Whether the excess is CTmvp.** Needs the Ivy GAP MVP/HBV image annotations, not a transcriptional proxy whose signature is the endothelial gene set.
4. **Section 2 remains the outlier on every test in (a)** — its endothelial programme and its held-out probes are all on the same immuno-oncology panel and none is as specific as PECAM1. That is a marker problem, not an aggregation or a density problem, and `results/classifier_fix.md` §6 item 1 already says no scoring rule can fix it.

## 7. What changed in the code

**Nothing.** This audit adds `tmesim/validation/endothelial_density.py` and this report. It calls `reconstruct/real_xenium.py`, `reconstruct/vessel_network.py`, `reconstruct/vessel_geometry.py`, `reconstruct/region_label.py` and `reconstruct/marker_panels.py` and modifies none of them; `core/`, `physics/` and `sim/` are untouched. The recommendations in §6 are deliberately left as recommendations.
